name: The Agia Solomoni wishing tree

location.address: Agia Solomoni Catacomb, Kato Paphos, Paphos

access: Free to enter the catacomb site (Guide to Paphos); the tree grows over the catacomb entrance and is seen from the railing at street level. Published hours conflict (daily 8:00 to 16:00 but also Sunday closed), check before going.
transport: In Kato Paphos, walkable from the harbour area; exact walking time and bus stop not checked
verify_notes: Flagged: age and girth not documented anywhere seen; species from one page only. Species: cyprusalive.com says 'a huge Terebinth tree above the catacomb' (no pistachio mention; Cyprus terebinths are sometimes P. atlantica, not settled). Tradition (all three pages): visitors hang coloured rags and cloth on its branches as offerings to Saint Solomoni; cyprusalive says many believe it cures eye problems, visitcyprus says it is believed to have curative powers; also called the Hankie or Wishing tree. It grows out of the stone catacomb complex directly above the entrance. ALIVE: Commons photos dated 2023-03-04 (Agia Solomoni Catacombs, Pafos, Kypr 01 and 02, CC BY-SA 4.0) show the multi-stemmed trunk, bare in March, loaded with rags, standing; viewed. PIN: Commons geotags (34.76168, 32.41247 and neighbours within 40 m, many files) cluster on the site; visitcyprus lists 34.761092, 32.424012 which is about 1.1 km east and wrong in longitude, ignore. Site is one small fenced catacomb court, the tree is the only large tree over it. Commons photo of the actual trunk, open licence: File:Agia Solomoni Catacombs, Pafos, Kypr 02.jpg (full tree and catacomb, CC BY-SA 4.0, 2023) and File:Agia Solomoni Catacombs, Pafos, Kypr 01.jpg (trunk and rags). lifecheck RECENT hit was an unrelated pine, not used. Not in the Forestry Department register. SECOND SOURCE (added): wotanland.blogspot.com, post dated 2024-07-11, visit July 2024 (earlier visit 2022), calls it a terebinth (Pistacia terebinthus), a large tree overhanging a wall on Fabrika Hill by the cave entrances, tied with hundreds of strips of cloth, scarves, masks and sometimes small padlocks; masonry built around the bole; confirms alive in July 2024. Same blog says the public areas are littered and graffitied and the spring entrance is roped off (the tree itself is visible from outside the fence). Species is now two-source (cyprusalive, wotanland), age still undocumented.

name: Aphrodite's Oak

location.address: Junction of the Aphrodite and Adonis nature trails, Akamas peninsula, near Neo Chorio, Paphos District

access: Open to walkers on the Aphrodite and Adonis nature trails in the Akamas protected area; no fee or gate found. Reached on foot only; komoot warns it is in a protected area, check local regulations.
transport: No public transport found; the trailhead area is by car near Neo Chorio/Aphrodite Baths, roughly 8 km west of Polis (not driven or checked)
verify_notes: Flagged: age undocumented, access/trailhead details thin. Identity: the Commons category 'Famous Quercus Infectoria, Neo Chorio' (geotag 35.059178, 32.326401; photos by Fry72, 2023-03-07, CC BY-SA 4.0, File:Famous Quercus Infectoria, Néo Chōrió, Cyprus 01 to 05.jpg) and the komoot highlight 'Aphrodite's Oak and Water Fountain' (35.05925, 32.326217) are the same tree, 16 m apart (not viewed). Independent sources: International Oak Society trip report, April-May 2026, calls the 'Aphrodite and Adonis oak' Q. infectoria subsp. veneris, trunk diameter 201 cm, canopy spread 28 m, standing alone in Mediterranean scrubland, intact branches, 'excellent vitality', 'the most impressive oak I encountered in Cyprus', at the fork of the Aphrodite and Adonis trails. girth_cm 631 is diameter 201 cm times pi (circumference at unstated height, from a trip report, not an official register). ALIVE: IOS report spring 2026; komoot tip 2026-10-10 'ancient oak with a very large trunk diameter at the junction of the Aphrodite and Adonis trail'; Commons 2023. AGE: no source. A komoot comment says 'French tree, 800 years old' (2022, unverified, almost certainly garbled, not usable). Not in the Forestry Department register as far as the register's village names show (Neo Chorio absent). PIN: lone tree at a trail junction, two independent coordinates (Commons geotag, komoot) within 16 m agree, so one clear crown; confirmed. Commons photo of the actual trunk: File:Famous Quercus Infectoria, Néo Chōrió, Cyprus 01.jpg (CC BY-SA 4.0, 2023-03-07). Another Commons file, Quercus infectoria subsp. veneris, Akamas Paninsula, Cyprus.jpg (Podzemnik, 2019, CC BY-SA 4.0), has no geotag, not matched to this tree.

name: The Simou village square terebinth

official_register.name: Cyprus Department of Forests, Tree Natural Monuments (data.gov.cy, CC BY 4.0)

access: Free; the tree stands in the public village square beside the church, with a taverna's outdoor tables in its shade (Cyprus Mail 2023).
transport: Village about 5 km northwest of Fyti in the hills; by car. Bus service not checked.
verify_notes: Flagged: register figures may belong to the other Simou entry; coordinates are the village's, not the tree's. REGISTER: Simou has two Forestry Department terebinths, CY-FD-26 (girth 615 cm, height 16 m, age 1008 yrs, proclaimed 2004-01-30) and CY-FD-73 (454 cm, 16 m, 500 yrs, proclaimed 2011-01-28). The one in the square is probably CY-FD-26, because yurtsincyprus calls the square tree 'over 1000 year old', but no source links the register id to the square tree, so girth 615 and height 16 are likely not certain; CY-FD-73 may stand elsewhere in the village (unchecked, lead). Register ages are round estimates carried to about 2012. Sources: yurtsincyprus.com says it is a Pistacia atlantica in Simou Village Square, over 1000 years old, with Panagia Chryseleousa church (built 1949) 'dominates the square and the village skyline'; Cyprus Mail restaurant review (2023-08-17) calls it a 'protected Pistacia Atlantica tree', 'colossal', complete shade, 'said to be the oldest tree in Cyprus', taverna O Tremythas on the same square, diners sit at tables outside under it, so alive in summer 2023; Wikipedia Simou says a tree in the village is said to be the oldest in Cyprus (cites terrabook, weak). The claim 'oldest in Cyprus' competes with Apesia (about 1,500 years, Cyprus Post centennial stamp, girth 6.8 m), do not repeat it for Simou. Age min/max reflect register 1008 vs 500 for the two Simou trees and the tourist 'over 1000'. PIN: Wikipedia village coordinates 34.94139, 32.50472 (village of about 170 people, the square is in the centre); tree-level position unknown. Terebinth in Cyprus is locally called tremithos. Not viewed; no Commons photo found (Commons search was rate-limited).
